answers.flag: Option A needs a stop at every resize while the stem allows stops only in the weekly window, so growth steps are tied to windows and the stem gives no ceiling on instance size, which leaves room to argue B (Auto Scaling group with min and max of 1 for self-healing) as the more elastic answer.

case.label: B
case.text: An Auto Scaling group is the AWS-native answer to changing load and growth, and a candidate can read 'minimal downtime' as favouring B because resizing in A stops the instance and cannot happen outside the weekly window, so peaks before the next window are unsolved. B could also be read as valid if the group is held at one instance (min=max=1) for replacement. However the stem says the application keeps in-memory state and cannot run as several copies, which makes scale-out unusable, so the case for B is weak but it is the obvious attractor for a pattern-matching candidate.
